scenarios.scenario: Deep — Full autonomous root cause investigation and fix proposal
scenarios.reasoning: The agent performed an excellent investigation. It efficiently extracted errors, traced the root cause through multiple log lines, identified the Debug/Release configuration mismatch caused by missing solution configuration entries, and proposed concrete fixes. The report is well-structured with specific line references backing every claim. The investigation was methodical — starting from errors, tracing to the failing target, then checking configurations. The agent also identified the cascading failure to LrgServiceServiceFabricTests. Minor improvements could include more explicit verification of the fix and clearer proof of absence from the solution config, but overall this is thorough, accurate, and well-presented work.

scenarios.scenario: Insight — Determine which projects are in the solution vs referenced
scenarios.reasoning: The agent performed extensive investigation (28 tool calls) and correctly identified the error (MSB3030), the missing file, and the Debug vs Release configuration mismatch. However, it got a critical part of the analysis wrong: it claimed LrgWindowsAppManifest was included in the solution with a Debug mapping, when the evidence (and rubric) indicate it was NOT in the solution at all and was only built as a P2P dependency. This led to an incorrect root cause explanation. The agent's own grep results showed the project wasn't in the initial deduplicated project list, but it didn't notice this discrepancy. While the surface-level diagnosis looks plausible, the underlying mechanism is wrong.

scenarios.scenario: Analysis — Diagnose why a file copy failed during build
scenarios.reasoning: The agent did solid investigative work in the binlog, correctly identifying the Debug vs Release configuration mismatch and the immediate mechanics of the failure. However, it stopped one level short of the true root cause: the reason the configuration wasn't propagated is that the referenced project isn't part of the solution file. This is a well-known MSBuild behavior — projects not in the .sln don't get solution-level configuration/platform mappings and fall back to defaults. The agent's fix suggestions are valid but miss the simplest and most correct fix (adding the project to the solution). The analysis is competent but incomplete on the deeper 'why'.
